words.definition: a specialized cell that receives, processes and transmits electrical or chemical signals in the nervous system
words.japanese: ニューロン・神経細胞
words.example: A neuron can conduct an action potential along its axon.

words.definition: the part of a neuron containing the nucleus and most organelles
words.example: The cell body maintains the neuron's metabolism.

words.definition: a branched extension of a neuron that receives signals from other cells
words.example: Dendrites increase the surface area available for receiving synaptic input.

words.definition: a long neuron process that conducts action potentials away from the cell body
words.example: An action potential travels along the axon toward terminal regions.

words.definition: a long projection of a neuron, usually an axon, that conducts nerve impulses
words.example: Myelination can increase conduction speed along a nerve fibre.

words.definition: an insulating lipid-rich layer wrapped around many axons
words.example: The myelin sheath reduces current loss from an axon.

words.definition: the voltage difference across a neuron's membrane when it is not transmitting an action potential
words.example: A neuron maintains a negative resting potential relative to its exterior.

words.definition: the electrical potential difference across a cell membrane
words.example: Ion distributions create the membrane potential of a neuron.

words.definition: a membrane protein that uses ATP to move sodium ions out of cells and potassium ions into cells
words.japanese: ナトリウム-カリウムポンプ
words.example: The sodium-potassium pump helps maintain ion gradients across neuronal membranes.

words.definition: Na+, a positively charged ion involved in membrane potentials and nerve signalling
words.example: Movement of sodium ions across neuronal membranes contributes to electrical signalling.

words.definition: K+, a positively charged ion important in maintaining and changing membrane potential
words.example: Potassium ion gradients contribute to the resting properties of neurons.

words.definition: a rapid, temporary change in membrane potential that propagates along an excitable cell membrane
words.example: An action potential carries information along an axon.

words.definition: a propagated electrical signal along a neuron, usually consisting of action potentials
words.japanese: 神経インパルス・神経興奮
words.example: A nerve impulse travels from a sensory neuron toward the central nervous system.

words.definition: the width of an axon
words.example: A larger axon diameter can increase conduction speed.

words.definition: the rate at which an electrical signal travels along a nerve fibre
words.example: Myelination and axon diameter affect conduction speed.

words.definition: a junction where a neuron communicates with another neuron or effector cell
words.example: Neurotransmitters carry signals across many synapses.

words.definition: the membrane of the signalling cell at a synapse
words.example: Neurotransmitter is released from the presynaptic side of a chemical synapse.

words.definition: the narrow gap between pre- and postsynaptic cells at a chemical synapse
words.example: Neurotransmitter diffuses across the synaptic cleft.

words.definition: a chemical messenger released by a neuron that binds receptors on a postsynaptic cell
words.example: Acetylcholine is a neurotransmitter at many synapses.

words.definition: the membrane of the receiving cell at a synapse
words.example: Receptors on the postsynaptic membrane bind neurotransmitter.

words.definition: a muscle or gland cell that carries out a response to a signal
words.example: A motor neuron can stimulate an effector cell such as a muscle fibre.

words.definition: a postsynaptic membrane change that makes generation of an action potential more likely
words.japanese: 興奮性シナプス後電位
words.example: An excitatory postsynaptic potential moves the membrane potential toward threshold.
